description: Compact programmable controller with 8 universal inputs, relay outputs and analog outputs, RS485 Modbus RTU (and Ethernet on the TCP-IoT): hardware I/O
source: Tecnolog, manual of the TCP line of controllers (Portuguese), section 8.2

sources.title: Manual dos CLPs Tecnolog linha TCP - TCP46, TCP46-24, TCP46EX, TCP46A, TCP-IoT e TCP17
sources.note: chapter 8, Modbus address tables, and the Modbus slave blocks of chapters 7 and 9

notes: Section 8.2 covers the TCP-IoT and the TCP17 (black and red versions). The TCP-IoT has 4 relay outputs and the TCP17 has 6, so DO5 and DO6 exist only on the TCP17; the TCP-IoT has one RS485 port (master or slave), the TCP17 has two (one master and one slave).

The access column of this table is a dash for every register, including the outputs, so the map marks them read-only. The analog input status values are not given, and the PDF text of the analog input rows is scrambled: the addresses follow the three-register pattern of the first row (value in two registers, then status).

Programmable controller: the tables below are the fixed hardware map. Any other data (set points, counters, results of the logic) is exposed by MDBS blocks in the user program made with TProg, at the registers chosen there; those are not listed. Writes outside the limits set in an MDBS block are ignored.
Floating-point values take two registers with the high word first (ABCD); 16-bit values keep AB. The address is sent as written, with no offset (20000 is protocol address 20000).

The Modbus RTU slave (RS485) and Modbus TCP/UDP (Ethernet, port 502) are enabled and configured in the web server of the controller (speed, parity, stop bits, address, transmission delay); the manual gives no factory values for the serial port. Functions 01 to 06 and 16 are supported by the master side; the manual does not list the slave functions.
Written from the manufacturer's manual; not tested on a device.
